text:
maria: Anyone else seeing 403s when the CI runner tries to promote canary -> prod? Started ~06:15 UTC.
maria: Deploy job log snippet:
```yaml
Step: promote-to-prod
status: failed
error: HTTP 403 Forbidden
message: "Request had insufficient authentication scopes. iam.serviceAccounts.actAs denied for serviceAccount:prod-deploy-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"
job_id: gha/12345
```
maria: This is blocking a release. Repro: run `gcloud auth print-identity-token --impersonate-service-account=ci-runner@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com --audiences=https://iam.googleapis.com/` then call the token exchange in the workflow.
devin: Got it. Which service account is doing the impersonation? ci-runner or the workflow's runner SA?
maria: The workflow uses the GitHub runner (serviceAccount: ci-runner@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com) to impersonate prod-deploy-sa@redwood-prod...
ken: Can you paste `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy prod-deploy-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com --project=redwood-prod` ? suspect missing binding.
maria: Policy excerpt:
```
bindings:
- role: roles/iam.serviceAccountUser
  members:
  - user:alice@redwood.com
# ci-runner binding missing
```
maria: We used to grant `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` to ci-runner on prod SA during the rollout; maybe it got removed during a policy cleanup.
sre-bot: Alert: last IAM change on prod-deploy-sa was 4876543001 by infra-automation@redwood.com
alex: For CI impersonation the minimal right is `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` on the target SA (or `roles/iam.serviceAccountUser` depending on flow). `iam.serviceAccounts.actAs` errors usually map to missing impersonation binding.
devin: If you're using Workload Identity Federation or OIDC pool, ensure the provider mapping is still present and the `aud` on the token matches. That would cause 401/403 variances.
maria: Quick try: adding binding now:
```
gcloud iam service-accounts add-iam-policy-binding prod-deploy-sa@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --member=serviceAccount:ci-runner@redwood-dev.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator --project=redwood-prod
```
maria: Applied. Retrying the workflow...
maria: ✅ Promotion job now shows 200 OK and tasks proceeded. Release moved to prod.
ken: Nice. Can we narrow the root cause? infra-automation change might have been an aggressive policy prune. We should reconcile automation rules.
alex: I'll open an audit ticket and add a guard in the IAM cleanup playbook to skip CI impersonation bindings (low risk of overprivilege) and add a test that simulates impersonation during PRs.
devin: Also adding a CI linter test that runs `gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy` on critical SAs and fails CI if expected bindings missing.
maria: I'll file a support escalation doc and include the job id + policy diff. Thanks all :raised_hands:
security-bot: Reminder: For least-privilege, prefer granting `roles/iam.serviceAccountTokenCreator` scoped to the specific target SA rather than broad project-level roles.
maria: Closing the thread — prod is green. If any follow-ups, ping me.
